title: Finite-free normalization of the ordinary tensor coefficient cone
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative ring in the scheme universe, and $d$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $H$ be ordinary constant realization with its prescribed universe lift followed by ordinary scalar extension along the normalized map $\underline A\to A_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-adic-tower-extraction]. For a completed module $M$, form the actual diagram $B(M)_n=M\otimes_{A_T}(A/I^{n+1})_T$, and the cone with point $M$ and projections $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Write $F_r(N)=N^{\operatorname{Fin}(r)}$. For every natural number $r$, the diagram $B(H(A^r))$ is isomorphic to the actual coefficient diagram [lem-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-adic-coefficient-limit] followed by $F_r$. There is also an isomorphism $H(A^r)\cong F_r(A_T)$, and its composite with each coordinatewise coefficient projection equals the tensor cone projection followed by the diagram isomorphism. Rank zero and the zero ring are included.

source.place: Tag 09C6, lemma-connected-adic-lisse, the displayed completed finite-projective quotient complex; Modules on Sites, Tags 093J--093M, and Cohomology on Sites, Tag 06YQ.

proof.text: The regular module of the lifted constant ring maps to the unit of its ring sheaf by the sheafification of the ring-unit sections. Its underlying additive map is locally bijective: after the additive sheafification unit its composite is the ring sheafification unit, which is locally bijective. Local surjectivity of the first unit and cancellation show local bijectivity of the map. Thus it is an isomorphism. The explicit lift/restriction of the original regular A-module is the lifted regular module by the identity linear equivalence.

Apply ordinary completed scalar extension to that isomorphism. Its specified object formula identifies the result with changeOfRings on the unit. The proved scalar-extension unit constraint identifies this with the completed-ring unit. No choice of a new coefficient object is made.

The additive realization preserves finite products. Map the explicit module product isomorphism piIsoPi, apply PreservesProduct.iso and apply the regular-unit comparison coordinatewise, obtaining e0:H(A^r)≅A_T^r. For each coefficient module B, tensorRight B also preserves finite products; e0, that product comparison, and the left unitors give eB:H(A^r) tensor B≅B^r. Compose with each product projection: the map is exactly (e0 followed by that projection) tensor id_B, followed by the left unitor. This proves naturality in B by tensor interchange and left-unitor naturality.

Whisker the resulting natural isomorphism by the actual coefficient diagram. For a coefficient projection q:A_T→B, compose the desired cone equation with every product projection. Tensor interchange, right-unitor naturality, left-unitor naturality, and equality of the unitors at the unit give e0 then q = rightUnitor inverse then id tensor q then eB. Product extensionality gives the cone equation, including the empty product.

theorem finitePerfectAdicFreeTensorCone_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (r : ℕ) :
    let M := (finitePerfectAdicOrdinary X d).obj (ModuleCat.of A (Fin r → A))
    let F : CompletedAdicModules X d ⥤ CompletedAdicModules X d :=
      Functor.const (Discrete (Fin r)) ⋙ lim
    ∃ (e : (finitePerfectAdicTensorFunctor X d).obj M ≅
        finitePerfectAdicCoefficientDiagram X d ⋙ F)
      (e₀ : M ≅ F.obj (SheafOfModules.unit (completedAdicRing X d))),
      ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ, e₀.hom ≫ F.map ((finitePerfectAdicCoefficientCone X d).π.app n) =
        (finitePerfectAdicTensorCone X d M).π.app n ≫ e.hom.app n
